name: Saint Barthélemy
summary: A French island, a Swedish free port, and a French island again.
notes: The 1784 treaty preceded Sweden’s 1785 takeover. The Order of Saint John held proprietary rights under French sovereignty. Some early British-occupation stories conflict with specialist archival accounts; no unsupported 1758–1764 interval is drawn.

events.title: Spain claims the island
events.detail: Columbus named the island after his brother’s patron saint.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: French settlement begins
events.detail: De Poincy sent colonists from Saint Kitts.

events.title: The Knights acquire proprietary rights
events.detail: The French company sold the administration to the Order of Saint John.

events.title: Settlement abandoned after an attack
events.detail: An Indigenous attack ended the first colonial settlement.

events.title: Colonists return
events.detail: Settlement resumed while the Order held proprietary rights.

events.title: French company administration resumes
events.detail: The sale of the Order’s rights was implemented.

events.title: English forces occupy the island
events.detail: An English expedition removed French settlers.

events.title: The settlement is abandoned
events.detail: The brief occupation was followed by evacuation.

events.title: French settlement renewed
events.detail: Colonial settlement resumed after the interruption.

events.title: British occupation
events.detail: The American Revolutionary War reached Saint Barthélemy.

events.title: French administration returns
events.detail: French forces displaced the British occupation.

events.title: France cedes the island to Sweden
events.detail: A treaty exchanged the island for commercial privileges in Gothenburg.

events.title: Sweden takes possession
events.detail: The first Swedish governor received the island from the French commandant.

events.title: Britain occupies the Swedish colony
events.detail: The anti-Danish and anti-neutrality campaigns reached the island.

events.title: France buys the island back
events.detail: An 1877 treaty and local vote preceded the formal handover to France.

events.title: A separate French collectivity
events.detail: The island separated administratively from Guadeloupe within France.
